chunks: Whoever has a debt and intends to repay it, Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, has with him two guardians who assist him in rendering the payment of his trust. But if his intention regarding repayment falls short, they fall short in assisting him in proportion to how much his intention falls short.

key_terms.أَمَانَتِهِ: his trust; the obligation owed to another
key_terms.الْأَدَاءِ: the act of fulfilling and rendering what is due
key_terms.حَافِظَانِ: two guardians appointed for protection and aid
key_terms.دَيْنٌ: a debt owed by a person

ai.seo_question: How does sincere intention to repay a debt affect divine help in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that sincere intention to repay a debt brings divine assistance. It emphasizes that fulfilling financial obligations is a trust, and that the degree of help a person receives corresponds to the truthfulness and strength of his intention.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3687 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:

"Whoever has a debt and intends to repay it, Allah (swt), the Mighty and Exalted, appoints two angels to assist him in fulfilling his trust. But if his intention to repay falls short, their assistance will also decrease in proportion to his intention."
